citation.title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network-based Topology Optimization (PINNTO) framework for structural optimization
citation.authors: Hyogu Jeong; Jinshuai Bai; Chanaka Batuwatta-Gamage; Charith Rathnayaka; Ying Zhou; YuanTong Gu
citation.version_coded: full-text author manuscript in QUT ePrints (repository item 237324)

included.method_family: other: physics-informed neural network used as an in-loop elasticity solver

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Across the initial validation cases, PINNTO's compliance is generally within about 2-3% of classical SIMP, with small shape differences.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Table 1, Case 1: classical SIMP total 0.81 s divided by PINNTO total 915.02 s = 0.000885; equivalently PINNTO takes about 1129.65 times as long. This is a secondary timing result, not the primary quality outcome.
claim.alternatives: Abstract says PINNTO produces designs comparable with SIMP without FE analysis; Section 4.1 Table 1 reports much longer PINNTO runtimes; Section 4.6 claims fewer TO iterations in one 3D example without a total runtime.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP compliance minimization with optimality-criteria updates (Sections 2.2 and 4.1)
baseline.implementation: 88-line MATLAB SIMP implementation for 2D validation; Liu and Tovar SIMP code for the 3D comparison (Sections 4.1 and 4.6)
baseline.hardware_classical: Intel Core i7-10700 CPU at 2.90 GHz, 16.0 GB DDR4 RAM for all numerical cases (Section 3.2)
baseline.hardware_ml: Intel Core i7-10700 CPU at 2.90 GHz, 16.0 GB DDR4 RAM; PyTorch 1.9.1+cpu (Section 3.2)
baseline.problem_size: 2 m x 1 m beam, 40 x 20 elements for four validation cases; 3D case uses 60 x 20 x 4 hexahedral elements (Sections 4.1 and 4.6)
baseline.classical_iterations: Cases 1-4: 35, 49, 67, and 11 TO iterations; convergence error threshold 0.01% (Section 4.1, Table 1)
baseline.classical_time: Cases 1-4: 0.81, 1.19, 1.56, and 0.31 s total; 0.02, 0.02, 0.02, and 0.03 s/iteration (Table 1)
baseline.training_time: not separately stated; PINN training is included within the reported per-problem PINNTO times (Section 3.2 and Table 1)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; no offline labeled dataset is used (Abstract and Section 3.2)
baseline.quality_metric: Mean compliance and prescribed volume fraction (Section 4.1, Table 1)
baseline.quality_gap: Table 1 Cases 1-4 report 0.02%, 2.92%, 1.28%, and 5.51% objective differences between PINNTO and SIMP

R1.evidence: Section 4.1 after Figure 7: selected outcome compares compliance similarity; speed is a separate result in Table 1.

R2.evidence: Section 4.1 and Table 1: both approaches ran on the stated CPU, and the classical SIMP implementation is identified; none of protocol R2(a)-(e) is established for this paper.

R3.evidence: Sections 3.1-3.2: the energy PINN is trained within each topology optimization run, with no offline pretraining or labeled training set.

R4.evidence: Sections 3.1 and 4.1: PINNTO computes the returned design's displacement and compliance using its PINN approximation; an independent FE evaluation of the returned PINNTO design is not reported. Figure 3 checks a preliminary displacement problem, not the final topology.

reporting.n_test_cases: Four 2D validation cases in Figure 7/Table 1, plus mesh/architecture/passive-element/multiple-load demonstrations and one 3D case (Sections 4.2-4.6)

notes: Full text read from QUT ePrints https://eprints.qut.edu.au/237324/1/122042111.pdf . The accessible full text is an author manuscript; the publisher version was not directly reachable. The paper states that PINNTO is substantially slower than SIMP on all four timed validation cases, despite describing faster iteration convergence in selected cases.
